facts.statement: The genus Vayuraptor contains only one known species, Vayuraptor nongbualamphuensis, which is known from a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Vayuraptor nongbualamphuensis, known from a partial skeleton.

facts.statement: Fossils of Vayuraptor were discovered in 1988 by Paladej Srisuk at Phu Wat Site A1 in Nong Bua Lamphu Province, Thailand, and are now stored in the Sirindhorn Museum.
facts.quote: The holotype and referred specimens of Vayuraptor (stored in the Sirindhorn Museum under the Department of Mineral Resources) were discovered in 1988 by Paladej Srisuk at Phu Wat Site A1, Nong Bua Lamphu Province, Thailand.

facts.statement: The generic name Vayuraptor means "wind thief", derived from the Hindu god of wind Vayu and the Latin word for thief.
facts.quote: The generic name means "wind thief", named after the Hindu god of wind Vayu and the Latin word raptor, which means thief.

facts.statement: The name Vayuraptor was chosen because its long and gracile tibia suggests the animal was very fast and agile.
facts.quote: This name was chosen because Vayuraptor possesses a long and gracile tibia, which suggests it was very fast and agile.

facts.statement: The specific name nongbualamphuensis is named after the Nong Bua Lamphu Province where the dinosaur was found.
facts.quote: The specific name is named after the province Vayuraptor was found in (Nong Bua Lamphu Province).

facts.statement: Vayuraptor was a mid-sized theropod estimated to be between 4 and 4.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Vayuraptor was a mid-sized theropod, estimated at 4-4.5 m in length.

facts.statement: As a possible megaraptoran, Vayuraptor likely had a long snout, large claws, a light body, and long slender legs.
facts.quote: As a possible megaraptoran, Vayuraptor would have had a long snout, large claws, light body, and long slender legs.

facts.statement: The left tibia of Vayuraptor is complete, long, and slender, featuring an expanded cnemial crest.
facts.quote: The left tibia is complete, long, and slender, with an expanded cnemial crest.

facts.statement: In a 2019 description, Novas et al. recovered Vayuraptor as a coelurosaurian in a trichotomy with megaraptorans and tyrannoraptorans.
facts.quote: En las descripción de 2019, lo agregaron al análisis de Novas et al. para recuperarlo ahora como un celurosauriano en una tricotomía con megaraptoranos y tyrannoraptoranos.

facts.statement: Vayuraptor likely shared its habitat with dinosaurs such as Phuwiangvenator, Kinnareemimus, Siamosaurus, Siamotyrannus, and Phuwiangosaurus.
facts.quote: With the first fossils of the genus being discovered in the Sao Khua Formation, Vayuraptor possibly shared its habitat with the dinosaurs Phuwiangvenator (which was also named in the same paper as Vayuraptor), Kinnareemimus, Siamosaurus, Siamotyrannus and Phuwiangosaurus.

facts.statement: Vayuraptor lived during the Barremian stage, approximately 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The manual phalanx of Vayuraptor lacks distinct extensor pits on the upper proximal surface, a trait found only in coelurosaurs.
facts.quote: No tiene pozos extensores distintos en la superficie superior proximal, más cerca del cuerpo, a la superficie de articulación distal, que es un rasgo que solo se encuentra en los celurosaurianos.

rejected.quote: Vayuraptor (meaning "wind thief") is an extinct genus of probable megaraptoran theropod dinosaur known from the Lower Cretaceous (Barremian) Sao Khua Formation of Thailand.
